newsitem.title: USA: Fed cheers slowdown, but not seen out of woods yet.
newsitem.headline: Fed cheers slowdown, but not seen out of woods yet.

text.p: The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged on Tuesday, suggesting the central bank is comfortable with the pace of the economic slowdown seen so far in the second quarter, former Fed officials said.
But central bank policymakers do not appear to be out of the woods just yet.

"Because the threat of inflation is not at all immediate, they had an opportunity, given by this slowdown on the economy, to wait and see what happens," said Lyle Gramley, a former Federal Reserve Board Governor.
Gramley, who correctely predicted the Fed's action on Tuesday, said he expected the economy to resume its exuberant course in the third quarter.
"My thought is that we are going to find the economy resuming much more rapid growth in the third quarter, and that eventually the Fed will have to raise rates significantly," Gramley said.
